subject: Scheduling: Tri-zone demo & security sync for NovaLabs
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novalabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer, marissa_cole, ben_carter
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novalabs.com>, security@novalabs.com
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Scheduling: Tri-zone demo & security sync for NovaLabs

Hi Karthik / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time to work with us. NovaLabs is keen to see Redwood running against a small production-like workload. We have stakeholders across US, EU and APAC who need to attend: our platform team (me), procurement (Tom), and our security group (security@novalabs.com).

We need two things:
- A 45–60 minute product demo (AE + SE present) that walks through latency, routing, and a short inference run.
- A 25–30 minute security Q&A (SOC2, data flows, SSO/SAML, KMS) — could be immediately after the demo or scheduled as a follow-up.

Time constraints: our EU engineering leads are only available during US mornings (their afternoons). APAC can join very late evenings PST. Ideally we rotate so the burden is shared across Redwood and NovaLabs teams.

Suggested date range: next week (July 20–24). Can you propose 3 options that cover each overlap window (US morning / EU afternoon / APAC evening)? Tom will need procurement steps and any invoice/PO requirements up front. I attached a short internal checklist for our side.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to narrow windows.

— Sarah
Sarah Chen
Platform Lead, NovaLabs
attachments: NovaLabs-MA-Checklist.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novalabs.com>, marissa_cole, ben_carter
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novalabs.com>, security@novalabs.com, priyom_das
Date: 2026-07-18T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Tri-zone demo & security sync for NovaLabs

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. We can definitely do a rotating plan so the same Redwood folks don't always take the late APAC slot. Proposed approach: one 60-minute demo (AE-led, SE technical deep-dive inside) + an optional 30-minute security add-on. Below are three slot bundles that each provide a reasonable overlap across the three regions; please confirm which bundle works for your stakeholders. All times shown in UTC, and with local conversions.

Option A — US-friendly (we lead from PST morning):
- Demo: 2026-07-21 16:00–17:00 UTC (08:00–09:00 PDT / 17:00–18:00 CEST / 00:00–01:00 SGT)
- Security add-on: 17:10–17:40 UTC

Option B — EU-friendly (middle ground):
- Demo: 2026-07-22 14:00–15:00 UTC (07:00–08:00 PDT / 15:00–16:00 CEST / 22:00–23:00 SGT)
- Security add-on: 15:10–15:40 UTC

Option C — APAC-inclusive (we rotate late):
- Demo: 2026-07-23 02:00–03:00 UTC (19:00–20:00 PDT previous day / 03:00–04:00 CEST / 10:00–11:00 SGT)
- Security add-on: 03:10–03:40 UTC

Logistics: I'll create a persistent meeting link and a rotating calendar series once you pick a bundle. Attendees we recommend: AE (me), SE (Marissa), Infra SE (Ben), Eng owners (Sarah and team), Procurement (Tom), Security rep.

Attachments: Redwood-Demo-Checklist.pdf (short runbook), plus our SOC2 link (see link below).

Next steps: please confirm preferred option and which specific people must be present for the demo vs security Q&A. If none of these bundles cover availability, tell us two concrete windows and we'll match.

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Adding a note on the SE side — thanks Sarah. For the demo I can cover: model routing, KV cache behavior, and an infra-oriented live run (we'll spin up a small model and run a 1k sequence test so you can see latency and memory). For the run we need:
- A laptop with SSH access to a sandbox (or screen-share and I'll run the test).
- Sample prompt suite (5–7 prompts) — if you can share one day ahead that's ideal.

Availability: I can do Option A mornings and Option B mid-days. Option C would push me late but I can rotate if we make it a recurring series and alternate who takes the late slot.

I also recommend a short pre-read (one pager) for your security folks that covers network flows and data residency — I can circulate that once we lock a time.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick procurement notes from my side:
- We need a formal quote and MoM-level SOW before we put a PO in. Can you send a standard quote template and indicate any promotional credits?
- For SSO: provide SAML metadata and a brief note on supported IdPs.
- For legal/security: copy of SOC2 (attested) and data retention policy.

If you can drop the quote + SOC2 PDF to me today/early tomorrow I can get internal approvals aligned with the demo. Our security team (cc'd) will join the security add-on 90% of the time.

— Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement, NovaLabs
